How many counties does Oregon have, and why does it matter when you sell?

Oregon has 36 counties, and nearly every step of a home sale runs through one of them. The county sets the tax bill, records the deed and holds the lien records a title company will search before closing.

The spread is wide. According to Wikipedia's county list, Multnomah County has 795,391 residents on 435 square miles, while Wheeler County has 1,472 residents and Harney County covers 10,135 square miles. A seller in Portland and a seller in Fossil deal with very different offices, so the first call is to your own county.

How do property taxes affect a sale in Oregon?

Any unpaid property tax has to be dealt with by closing, so check the balance with your county before you accept an offer. Oregon taxes are billed at county level, and each county runs its own payment site.

Multnomah County's payment page gives a clear picture of the installment pattern. Payment in full by November 15 earns a 3 percent discount. Paying two thirds by that date earns 2 percent, with the last third due May 15. Paying only one third brings no discount, and the later installments fall on February 15 and May 15. Late payments accrue interest at 1.3333 percent per month, and the page notes that payments must be received or postmarked by the due date to qualify for a discount. Other counties may differ, so confirm with the office that mails your bill.

  • Pull your most recent statement and look for any unpaid installment.
  • Ask the county tax office for a payoff figure good through your expected closing date.
  • Tell the title company if a mortgage servicer has been paying taxes from escrow.

Our state-level write-up on Oregon property taxes goes deeper, and we have county guides for places such as Multnomah, Washington and Clackamas.

Is foreclosure in Oregon judicial or non-judicial?

Oregon allows both, but most home loans use a trust deed, and a trust deed can be foreclosed outside court by advertisement and sale under ORS chapter 86. A lender can also choose a judicial foreclosure, which goes through a lawsuit under ORS 88.010.

The timeline is longer than many owners expect. Once a notice of default is recorded, the notice of sale must reach the borrower and others with recorded interests at least 120 days before the trustee sells the property (ORS 86.764). A borrower, a successor in interest or a junior lienholder can cure the default up to five days before the last scheduled sale date by paying what is owed plus costs. For a residential trust deed, the combined trustee and attorney fees in that cure are capped at $1,000, or the actual amount if it is less (ORS 86.778).

Two rules matter if you are thinking about selling instead of waiting:

  • A trustee's sale ends the interest of people who received notice, and they cannot redeem the property from the buyer (ORS 86.797).
  • After a trustee's sale or a judicial foreclosure of a residential trust deed, the lender generally cannot sue for a deficiency (ORS 86.797).

A sale before the auction date can stop the process and keep the foreclosure off your record. Judgment creditors are a separate track. Our page on Oregon sheriff sales covers execution sales and the redemption window that follows them.

What happens to an inherited house in Oregon?

The house goes through the estate unless a transfer on death deed or a trust already names who receives it. Oregon has a simplified route for small estates called a simple estate affidavit, which ORS 114.505 defines and ORS 114.515 sets out. Larger or more complicated estates usually go through a formal probate with a personal representative.

The person who can sign for the estate is the one to talk to before any sale. Title companies typically ask for court papers or an affidavit that shows who has authority, and county records must match.

If a transfer on death deed was recorded, the process can look quite different. We explain both routes on our probate page and our transfer on death deed page. The tax side of an estate is covered in our write-up on Oregon estate tax.

Heirs who live out of state often sell as-is, since repairing a house from a distance is slow.

How do deeds and recording work in Oregon?

A deed that conveys fee title must state the true consideration paid, and a recording officer may not accept it without that statement (ORS 93.030). Leaving it out does not invalidate the conveyance on its own, but the county can refuse to record the paper, which stalls a closing.

Recording happens at the county clerk's office, and your title or escrow officer usually handles the filing. Before changing names on a deed ahead of a sale, check the details. Our guide to the Oregon quitclaim deed explains what that form transfers and what it leaves unanswered.

We did not open a state source on transfer tax, so we are not stating a rate here. Ask the title company at the start of your sale which fees apply in your county.

Does the Oregon homestead exemption protect my house from a sale?

The homestead exemption protects part of your home's value from creditors who hold a judgment against you. It is a debt rule, not a property tax break. Under ORS 18.395, the exemption applies without the owner filing a claim, and the home must be the actual abode of the owner or the owner's spouse, parent or child.

Three details matter to a seller:

  • The exemption can follow sale proceeds for up to one year if the money is held with the intent to buy another homestead.
  • For a judgment of $3,000 or less at the time of entry, an occupied homestead cannot be sold on execution (ORS 18.395(5)).
  • The dollar limits were changed by a 2024 law, SB 1595, so older printed figures are out of date. Check the current amount with the Oregon Judicial Department or an attorney.

For the full picture, see our page on the Oregon homestead exemption.

What if my Oregon house has tenants?

You generally need a legal reason and the right notice period to end a tenancy for a sale. The rules sit in ORS 90.427, and they depend on how long the tenant has lived there and what kind of tenancy it is.

SituationWhat the statute says
Month-to-month, first year of occupancyLandlord may end it with at least 30 days' written notice
Month-to-month after the first yearOnly for tenant cause or a qualifying landlord reason
Accepted offer from a buyer who will live thereAt least 90 days' notice, plus written evidence of the offer within 120 days of accepting it
Same property as the landlord's home, two units or fewer30 days' notice if a buyer will occupy the unit
Termination that breaks the rulesLiability for three months' rent plus actual damages

A landlord who ends a tenancy for a qualifying reason must also pay one month's rent when delivering the notice, unless the landlord owns four or fewer residential units (ORS 90.427). Some cities add their own rules; a court annotation on the statute mentions a Portland relocation assistance ordinance. Many owners of rented houses choose to sell with the tenant in place. Read our pages on the eviction process and landlord and tenant law before sending any notice.

What does a cash sale as-is mean in Oregon?

It means the buyer agrees to take the house in its current condition and pays without a mortgage contingency. You do not fix the roof, clear the garage or repaint before closing. Closing still goes through a title or escrow company, which checks the deed, pays off liens and records the transfer.

Sellers who call us are often dealing with one of these situations:

  • A house inherited from a parent, with a probate or affidavit step still open.
  • Back taxes or a loan in default, with a trustee sale on the calendar.
  • A rental with a tenant, or a vacant property that needs work.
  • A move on short notice, such as a job change.

We explain what we look at, and how closing works, on each city page. Start with the biggest metros, such as Salem, Eugene, Bend and Medford, or find your county below. If your property is in a smaller place we do not list, send us the address anyway.

Frequently asked questions

How many counties are in Oregon?

Oregon has 36 counties, per Wikipedia's county list.

How long does an Oregon trustee sale take?

Notice of sale must go out at least 120 days before the trustee sells. You can cure the default up to five days before the last scheduled sale date.

Can I sell my Oregon house if it is in foreclosure?

Yes. A sale before the trustee's sale can pay off the loan. After the sale, people who got notice cannot redeem.

Do I owe property tax at closing in Oregon?

Unpaid tax is settled at or before closing. Ask your county for a payoff figure.

Can I sell an inherited house before probate ends?

It depends on who has legal authority. A personal representative or a simple estate affidavit signer can usually act, and the title company will want proof.

Can I sell a rented house with the tenant there?

Yes, many owners do. If the buyer will live there, ORS 90.427 sets 90 days' notice with written evidence of the offer.

Does a cash sale as-is mean no repairs?

Yes. The buyer takes the house in its current condition, and a title or escrow company handles the paperwork.
